data.description:
Three defects the operator hit on the public agenda of the live site (https://marquee.stage11.dev, 2026-08-11). They share two files, so they are one ticket and one PR — three agents editing `PublicAgendaPage.tsx` would collide. The public agenda is the conference's front door and sits on the walkthrough path. --- ## 1. The agenda defaults to day one and then blames the user for it **Operator:** *"nothing has happened when I click show full agenda. Just says no published sessions match. Clear a filter. But I've got no filter set."* Root cause, `src/lib/public-site.ts:486`: const selectedDay = filters.allDays ? null : filters.day ?? event.startsOn; With **no query parameters at all**, `filters.day` is null, so `selectedDay` silently becomes `event.startsOn` — day one. A visitor who has set nothing is served a day-filtered agenda without being told. If day one has no published sessions, the page reports an empty conference. It compounds three ways: - **The empty state lies.** `PublicAgendaPage.tsx:226` computes `hasFilters = Boolean(track || q || (day && day !== "all"))`. The defaulted day makes this true, so the visitor is told *"No published sessions match — clear a filter to bring the program back into view"* when they never set a filter and the UI shows none set. - **"Show full agenda" is a no-op.** That button links to `/agenda?${eventQuery}` — i.e. `/agenda?event=` — which carries no `day`, so the server re-applies the identical day-one default and renders the byte-identical page. Clicking it does nothing, forever. This is exactly what the operator saw. - **"All days" is unreachable.** The code has an `allDays` path (signalled by `day=all`), but the day tablist at `PublicAgendaPage.tsx:194-200` renders only concrete days. There is no control that produces `day=all`, so a visitor can never get to the full program through the UI. **Required outcome.** Decide the correct default and make it honest: - Showing the **whole program by default** is almost certainly right for a conference front door — a visitor who lands on "Agenda" wants the agenda. If you instead keep a day default, the UI must *show* that day as selected so it does not read as an empty conference. **Pick one, justify it in one sentence in the PR, and make the UI state and the server state agree either way.** - Add an **"All days"** control to the day tablist, reflecting selected state like the other tabs. - `hasFilters` must be true only for filters the visitor actually chose. A defaulted value is not a filter. - "Show full agenda" must clear every filter, day included, and visibly change the page. If a click can't change the result, the button must not be there. - Keep the genuinely-empty case honest: an unpublished program still says "No published sessions yet", not "no match". ## 2. A raw JSON endpoint is linked from the public conference site `PublicAgendaPage.tsx:190`: Agenda data ↗ This sits next to the page's `

` and dumps a JSON object in the visitor's face. **Operator: we shouldn't show that.** Remove the link from the public agenda page. Do **not** remove the `/api/v1/public/agenda` endpoint itself — it is a real public API, it is documented in `src/routes/public.routes.ts:36`, and the embed feature depends on that surface. This is about not advertising a developer artifact to conference attendees. The "Get embed code" action in the shell is the legitimate integrator path and stays. ## 3. There is no way back out of the agenda **Operator:** *"when looking at the agenda, there's no way for me to go back to the page that I was on."* `PublicShell` (`PublicAgendaPage.tsx:128-152`) gives the visitor: a brand link to `/agenda`, "Get embed code", and "Organizer demo". From the agenda page the brand link is a self-link — pressing the one thing that looks like "home" reloads the page you are on. There is no route back to the conference landing page, and the session (`/s/:slug`) and speaker (`/p/:slug`) detail pages inherit the same shell. **Required outcome.** The public shell gets a real, always-available way home — the brand should lead to the conference landing page (`/`), not to `/agenda`, and detail pages should offer a clear route back to the agenda. Every public page must be escapable using only what is on screen. Do not rely on the browser back button; a visitor who arrived by deep link has no history to go back to. --- ## Constraints - Flight Deck aesthetic per `DESIGN.md`; reuse existing `public-*` classes. - **Elements never jump** (global UI rule): adding the "All days" tab must not reflow the day tablist as selection changes; reserve width. - The agenda is server-rendered — check `src/routes/public-agenda.route.tsx` and `src/lib/public-site.ts` together so the UI and the query agree. - `src/ui/embeds/EmbedPage.tsx` carries the **same** `hasFilters` / "Show full agenda" pattern (lines 224-231). Verify whether it has the same no-op defect and fix it consistently if so; note the finding in the PR either way. - Speed is a graded feature (R7) — the agenda must stay fast. - Suite budget 45s, gate budget 120s. ## Acceptance - Loading `/agenda` with no query parameters shows the published program, and the day control visibly reflects whatever scope is being shown. - The "no filter set" empty state never says "clear a filter". - Clicking "Show full agenda" measurably changes the page, or the button is absent. - "All days" is reachable from the UI and works. - No JSON-endpoint link appears anywhere on the public agenda; `/api/v1/public/agenda` still responds and the embed flow still works. - From `/agenda`, `/s/:slug`, and `/p/:slug`, a visitor can reach the conference home in one click, and the brand link is never a self-link. - Validated on the **live deployed site** with screenshots in the PR — including the before/after of the empty-state case that started this ticket. - `npm test` green within budget; PR open against `Stage-11-Agentics/marquee` `main`.
data.title: Public agenda: day-one default fakes an empty conference, "Show full agenda" is a no-op, JSON link is exposed, and there is no way home

data.body: Baseline npm test: 68/69 files passed, 424/425 tests passed in 17.115s (within 45s budget). The sole failure is pre-existing MRQ-74 delivery-health quota setup, with missing RESEND_API_KEY warnings; no MRQ-94 code was changed.

BLOCKED before plan write: the shared /Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/deployments/Marquee checkout changed from mrq-91-venue-map to the active root worktree on mrq-93 during this session. I will not edit or commit in the shared checkout; need an isolated MRQ-94 worktree or operator-safe branch decision.

Brief correction sent to this delegator (2026-08-11): there is no auto-deploy on
this project — merging does not ship (see the new `DEPLOY.md`). My original boot
brief told every delegator to "validate against the live deployed site", which was
wrong: an unmerged branch is not on marquee.stage11.dev, and six delegators each
deploying their own branch to the judge-facing site the day before the deadline
would trample each other.

Standing rule for this ticket: validate **locally** with browser automation, read
the live site only to reproduce the original defect, and state in the PR that the
change still needs a deploy to reach production. Do not run `wrangler deploy`.

Implementation checkpoint: commit 11cab1b in isolated worktree mrq-94-public-agenda. Local Wrangler Worker on 127.0.0.1:8795 with synthetic seed, driven through c11 embedded browser. Observed /agenda showing the published program with All days active and no JSON link; q=zzzz-no-match showing the honest filtered-empty state; Show full agenda removing the query and restoring sessions; session and speaker details exposing / and <- Agenda. Screenshots captured locally for the PR. No deploy performed. npm test was green at 78 files / 496 tests / 26.050s, within the 45s suite budget; trace:ac is clean at 216 live criteria, 0 uncovered, 0 errors.

Rebased onto github/main 9e1636c; npm ci passed. Exact local build c942c64 reports health 200 on 127.0.0.1:8795. Re-drove the c11 browser flow on that build: default agenda All days active, no public API link, filtered empty state, reset restoring sessions, and session/speaker home plus agenda links all observed. Screenshots were refreshed from the rebased local build. No deployment performed.
